question_stem:
A nichrome resistance wire has length 150 cm, cross-sectional area 2.45 × 10^{-7} m^{2} and resistivity
1.12 × 10^{-6} Ω m.
question_stem_latex:
A nichrome resistance wire has length 150 cm, cross-sectional area $2.45 \times 10^{-7}\,\mathrm{m}^{2}$ and resistivity
$1.12 \times 10^{-6}\,\mathrm{\Omega}\,\mathrm{m}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question_text:
Calculate, to three significant figures, the resistance of the wire.
resistance = Ω
parts.question_text_latex:
Calculate, to three significant figures, the resistance of the wire.
$resistance = \Omega $

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
The nichrome wire forms part of a potentiometer circuit together with a cell of electromotive
force (e.m.f.) 1.2 V and negligible internal resistance, as shown in Fig. 7.1.
The circuit is used to determine the e.m.f. of cell X.
The galvanometer is used in a null method to find the null point 64 cm from the left-hand end
of the nichrome wire.
parts.question_text_latex:

The circuit is used to determine the e.m.f. of cell X.
The galvanometer is used in a null method to find the null point 64 cm from the left-hand end
of the nichrome wire.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.question_text: Explain what is meant by a null method.
parts.question_text_latex: Explain what is meant by a null method.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.question_text:
Calculate the e.m.f. of cell X.
e.m.f. = V
parts.question_text_latex:
Calculate the e.m.f. of cell X.
e.m.f. = V

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.question_text:
The cell of e.m.f. 1.2 V is replaced by a new cell with the same e.m.f. but with an internal
resistance that is not negligible.
State and explain the effect, if any, of the internal resistance of the new cell on the
position of the null point.
